bindings.label: A 7-year-old boy presented with behavioral issues since infancy.

Early developmental history: first child, unplanned pregnancy, oligohydramnios at 36 weeks, possible congenital cardiac defects noted in fetus; delivered preterm at 36 weeks via emergency cesarean section due to fetal bradycardia; birth weight 1.7 kg, delayed cry, and cyanosed at birth; cardiac evaluation at birth identified patent ductus arteriosus, ventricular septal defect, tricuspid regurgitation, and a left atrium to right atrium shunt, and he was started on digitoxin.

As he grew, he exhibited global developmental delay and was diagnosed with bilateral profound sensorineural hearing loss at 6 months of age; over time he continued to show delayed milestones and developed poor eye contact, poor social and communication skills, repetitive head rocking, hand flapping movements, and a preference for fixed routines.

From the age of 3, he displayed symptoms of attention deficit hyperkinetic disorder (ADHD), including an inability to sit still for more than 2-3 minutes and difficulty engaging in activities; his insistence on routine and hyperactivity increased over the years, leading to aggressive behaviors such as hitting and biting his mother, which resulted in significant distress and a psychiatry consultation with subsequent admission to a child psychiatry inpatient unit; there was no history of head injury, seizures, frequent diarrhea and vomiting, birthmarks, or failure to thrive.

Physical examination revealed a small head circumference (49 cm) and bilateral flat feet; mental status examination showed a lack of eye contact, hyperactivity, irritable mood, frequent side-to-side head movements, and hand flapping; his intelligence quotient was evaluated to be 25.
Brain MRI shows multifocal symmetric T2/FLAIR hyperintensities
Genetic/metabolic disorder with retinal and white matter involvement (possible leukodystrophy)
The patient exhibits the classic congenital rubella triad: sensorineural hearing loss, pigmentary retinopathy, and patent ductus arteriosus
